report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of drift.py: scan(), Acceptance, parse_acceptances, DriftItem, DriftReport. Verified docstring claims against code; all checkable claims kept, some uncheckable due to missing constants/definitions.
risks: parse_acceptances | medium | Uses MIN_WHY_CHARS, MAX_HORIZON_DAYS, and _drift_key from elsewhere; if these are not defined or have different semantics, the validation and drift key generation could diverge from intent. | Check the definitions of these names in the rest of the file.

scan | medium | Docstring claims 'no clock', but calls repo_state(probe_dirty=probe_dirty) which may access the filesystem and possibly the clock; the claim is broader than the code can verify in this chunk. | Inspect repo_state's implementation to confirm it does not use the clock.

scan | low | The dark switch filter skips 'secret' kind and documented switches; the docstring does not state this, so the behaviour may be surprising. | Confirm the intended policy in the module's documentation.

parse_acceptances | low | The 'since' future check uses 'today' even when the acceptance is already expired; the error message may be misleading for expired acceptances. | Test with an acceptance that is both expired and has a future 'since'.

handoff.purpose: Implements scan() to build architecture state, Acceptance dataclass with validation, parse_acceptances() with fail-closed parsing, and DriftItem/DriftReport dataclasses for reporting.

symbols.name: scan
symbols.note: Pure function deriving architecture state; accepts optional injected reports; no writes, clock, or network per docstring.

symbols.name: Acceptance
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for an acceptance; has valid property and expired() method.

symbols.name: Acceptance.valid
symbols.note: Property returning True if problem is empty.

symbols.name: Acceptance.expired
symbols.note: Returns True if today > until (ISO date parse); on ValueError returns True.

symbols.name: Acceptance.as_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict with item, why, since, until; includes who if non-empty.

symbols.name: parse_acceptances
symbols.note: Parses raw list into Acceptance objects, fail-closed; validates dates, horizon, why length; sorts by item, until, since.

symbols.name: DriftItem
symbols.note: Dataclass for a drift item; has blocking property and as_dict method.

symbols.name: DriftItem.blocking
symbols.note: False if kind in NON_BLOCKING_KINDS, else not accepted.

symbols.name: DriftItem.as_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict representation of the item.

symbols.name: DriftReport
symbols.note: Dataclass for the drift report; has blocking property returning list of blocking items.

symbols.name: DriftReport.blocking
symbols.note: Returns [i for i in items if i.blocking].

claims.text: Pure: no writes, no clock, no network.
claims.why: scan() calls repo_state() which may access the filesystem and possibly the clock; the claim cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: ``reach_report`` and ``switch_report`` may be injected by a caller that already built them (``daedalus map`` does, and that is the point: the page and the gate are then provably looking at the same analysis, not at two that happen to agree).
claims.why: The code checks `if reach_report is None:` and `if switch_report is None:` and only then builds them; injected reports are used as-is.

claims.text: ``index`` is only forwarded to reach for its structural cross-check.
claims.why: The code passes `index=index` only to `reach_mod.analyse(root, index=index)`; it is not used elsewhere in scan().

claims.text: The state also records WHICH TREE it was derived from (:func:`repo_state`).
claims.why: The state dict includes `"repo_state": repo_state(root, probe_dirty=probe_dirty)`.

claims.text: TEST ONLY is a property of an UNREACHED module, not of an island specifically.
claims.why: The code computes `unreached_facts` from `UNREACHED_CLASSES` and then `test_only` from `unreached_facts` with `m.tested_by`, not from islands only.

claims.text: An absent API key is not a dark feature.
claims.why: The code skips switches with `sw.kind == "secret"` before adding to dark.

claims.text: A module the scanner could not parse contributes nothing to either engine's answer, which makes it a hole in the map that used to be filled by a bare ``continue``. It is a finding, not a shrug.
claims.why: The code collects unparsable modules from both reach and switch reports into a set and includes them in the state counts and sites.

claims.text: Fail closed: anything we cannot fully validate is kept, marked with a ``problem``, and suppresses nothing.
claims.why: Every entry (even malformed) is appended as an Acceptance with a problem string; no entry is dropped.

claims.text: A typo in an acceptance must never be the thing that makes an island invisible.
claims.why: Malformed entries are kept with a problem and not suppressed; the code never filters out entries with problems.

claims.text: ``today`` binds the horizon to the CALENDAR. Without it the only rule is ``until - since <= MAX_HORIZON_DAYS``, which a pair of dates in 2999 satisfies while suppressing forever; the cap measured the acceptance against itself and nothing measured it against now.
claims.why: The code only checks `d_since > today` when `today` is provided; otherwise it skips that check. The horizon check is independent of today.

claims.text: Omitting ``today`` keeps the date-shape and horizon checks and skips only that one, so a caller that genuinely has no clock (``--accept`` validating a candidate before writing it) still gets everything else.
claims.why: The code performs date-format and horizon checks regardless of `today`; only the `since > today` check is conditional on `today` being truthy.

claims.text: Which tree the SNAPSHOT was generated against, versus the one just scanned. Reported, never blocking: a baseline taken one commit ago is not a defect, and a gate that goes red on every commit is a gate people switch off.
claims.why: The comment describes the purpose of the `freshness` field; the code only defines the field, not how it is used or reported. The claim about non-blocking is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: The consumers that RANK WORK out of these lists are the ones that must fail closed on it -- see :func:`snapshot_freshness`.
claims.why: The comment references `snapshot_freshness` which is defined elsewhere; the claim about consumers failing closed cannot be verified here.

observations.what: scan() docstring claims 'no clock' but calls repo_state(probe_dirty=probe_dirty) which may touch the filesystem and potentially the clock; the claim is broader than what this chunk can verify.
parse_acceptances() uses constants MIN_WHY_CHARS and MAX_HORIZON_DAYS that are not defined in this chunk; their values affect validation.
scan() uses _drift_key(entry) and _MIN_ABBREV, which are not defined in this chunk; the correctness of site keys and freshness checks depends on them.
DriftReport.blocking returns a list, not a boolean; the property name might be ambiguous but the code is clear.
